body: did you know: half the people who loved "blank space" missed the joke. taylor wrote it as satire of her own tabloid caricature -- "a girl who's crazy but seductive but glamorous but nuts but manipulative" -- and has said only about half of listeners caught it. it worked anyway: after debuting at no. 18 it knocked her own "shake it off" from no. 1 in week three -- the first time a woman replaced herself atop the hot 100 in the chart's 56-year history. seven straight weeks at no. 1.
why: X-native (text-only) sibling of the 1989 'Blank Space' did-you-know, keeping X active the same evening and filling the coldest era corner (1989 has zero recent coverage). Trimmed to the punchiest facts: the satire framing, her 'crazy but seductive...' caricature quote, ~half of listeners missing the joke, the No. 18 debut, replacing her own 'Shake It Off' at No. 1 in week three, and being the first woman in Hot 100 history to succeed herself at the top.
